named_events.loss_description: Material losses from the Caribbean and from the earthquakes in Mexico; contributed materially to 2017 underwriting deterioration
Material losses from the Caribbean referenced as part of the September 2017 catastrophes
Earthquakes in Mexico cited as a material loss driver in 2017

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2017 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 12.607m. Prioryear development (for underwriting years older than the two most recent) produced a small favourable movement of GBP 0.434m (a ~3.4% release relative to opening gross claims outstanding), driven by favourable claims development and recoveries on older years. By contrast, 2017 saw large gross reserve increases concentrated in Property driven by September 2017 catastrophe activity (Caribbean and Mexico earthquakes), which materially worsened 2017 underwriting results.
raw_causal_phrases: The key driver of claims is the unprecedented levels of CAT activity on the Property account.
material losses from the Caribbean and from the earthquakes in Mexico

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (Claims outstanding) prior-year column (2016). Prior year development derived from the gross claims development table (triangle) - only 2015 qualified as 'prior' after excluding the two most recent underwriting years (2017 & 2016); the triangle yields a small favourable movement of GBP 0.434k (i.e. GBP 0.434m). No explicit sentence quantifying a GROSS prior year movement was found in narrative text; exact_reserve_text therefore left empty. Named catastrophe events are referenced but not quantified for their individual gross reserve impacts.
